agents.infoText: Agents are AI assistants that handle tasks for you. Each agent has an identity, an LLM model, and access to specific tools. Create a new agent, assign tools, and configure its behavior. Open the other tabs to manage tools, federation, and blueprints.
agents.title: Agent management with runtime, skill and log focus
agents.subtitle: This area organizes agent profiles, heartbeats, direct chats, skills and logs into a clearer operational view. The functions remain the same, but the interface now separates analysis, configuration and runtime more clearly.

projects.infoText: A project connects a boss agent with worker agents. The boss coordinates tasks and delegates to workers. a2a.title: Federation (A2A)
a2a.subtitle: Connect this HydraHive instance to others in the network. Agents can use remote_agent to delegate tasks to peers.
a2a.incomingSecretDesc: Peers must send this secret in the X-A2A-Secret header to reach us.
a2a.peerSecretHint: the secret we send to this peer
a2a.toolUsageDesc: Add remote_agent to an agent's tools to enable peer access:
a2a.infoText: Federation lets you connect multiple HydraHive instances. Agents can then communicate and delegate tasks across instance boundaries.
a2a.guideTitle: How to connect two HydraHive nodes:
a2a.step1: Activate Tailscale on both instances (Settings → VPN) and make sure both are in the same tailnet
a2a.step2: Copy your instance's Tailscale IP and share it with the other user
a2a.step3: Click 'Add Peer' and enter the Tailscale IP of the other node
a2a.step4: The other user does the same with your IP — both sides must add each other as peers
a2a.step5: Test the connection with the 'Test' button. If successful, agents can communicate via the 'remote_agent' tool

brain.infoText: The 3D graph shows all agents, tools, projects and their connections. Rotate with the mouse, zoom with the scroll wheel, click nodes for details. Colors: Blue = Agents, Green = Tools, Orange = Projects, Purple = Memory.

heartbeat.infoText: Heartbeat tasks are automatic jobs your agent runs on a schedule — e.g. checking emails, creating reports, or monitoring systems. You define a message (the task) and a schedule.
heartbeat.helpMessage: The instruction your agent receives — write it like you'd brief a colleague
heartbeat.helpCron: Schedule in cron format. Examples: '0 8 * * *' = daily at 8:00, '*/30 * * * *' = every 30 minutes, '0 9 * * 1' = Mondays at 9:00
heartbeat.helpInterval: Alternative to cron: interval in seconds (e.g. 1800 = every 30 minutes)
